title: The Venmo of Mexico: How to Pay Anyone in Pesos from Your USD Account
summary: Money without borders. Send, spend, and save across borders with Blaze, built for nomads, expats, and global businesses.
body_markdown:
You just got to Mexico City. Apartment is great, neighborhood is perfect, and your landlord is super chill — except for one thing.


"Solo acepto transferencia bancaria o efectivo."


Bank transfer or cash only. No Venmo. No Zelle. Definitely not PayPal.


You open your US bank app, look up international wire transfers, and find: $35 fee, 3–5 business days, and you need their full CLABE number. You ask your landlord for their CLABE. They send it. You copy it wrong. You start over.


This is the reality of paying for things in Mexico from a US account — or at least, it used to be.


---


## 🇲🇽 Why "Just Venmo Me" Doesn't Work Here


Venmo is US-only. Cash App is US-only. Zelle barely works for sending to Mexico even when both parties have accounts.


Mexico runs on its own payment rails — primarily **SPEI** (Sistema de Pagos Electrónicos Interbancarios), the real-time interbank transfer system. When your landlord says "transferencia bancaria," they mean SPEI.


To send a SPEI transfer, you need a Mexican bank account. Or you need an app that bridges the two worlds.


---


## ⚡ How Blaze Solves This


Blaze lets you send money from your USD balance directly to any Mexican bank account via SPEI. The recipient gets pesos instantly — you spend dollars.


The fee: **0.5% flat.** No wire fee on top, no rate markup, no "international transfer surcharge."


On a $1,200 rent payment: that's $6.


Compare that to a bank wire ($35 fee + 3–5 days) and the difference isn't just money — it's the difference between a landlord who trusts you and one who's chasing you down.


> **Your landlord doesn't need to download anything. You send from Blaze, they receive a standard SPEI deposit in pesos. That's it.**


---


## 🏠 Use Case: Paying Rent


Your rent is 15,000 MXN/month. You hold USD. Here's what that looks like:


1. Open Blaze, tap Send
2. Enter your landlord's CLABE number
3. Enter the amount (in pesos or dollars — you choose)
4. Confirm the 0.5% fee
5. Hit send


It lands in their account in seconds. You get a receipt. They get a SPEI notification. Done.


No trips to a money exchange. No carrying cash. No $35 wire fee.

## 🤝 Use Case: Splitting Bills with Mexican Friends


Your friend group in CDMX is a mix of locals and expats. After a long dinner in Coyoacán, someone picks up the tab and everyone pays them back.


If your friends have a Mexican bank account — which most locals do — you can send them pesos directly from Blaze. You pay in USD, they receive in pesos, the exchange happens instantly at a fair rate.


No app downloads required on their end if you use a payment link. No awkward "do you have Venmo?" conversations.


---


## 🔨 Use Case: Paying a Contractor or Housekeeper


A lot of people living in Mexico hire local help — a housekeeper, a handyperson, a private Spanish tutor. These folks typically have a bank account or at least a CLABE.


Paying them weekly or biweekly via Blaze costs you 0.5%. Paying via bank wire would cost you $35 each time — which, for a $200 weekly payment, would be a 17.5% fee.


> **For recurring payments to people in Mexico, Blaze isn't just convenient — it's the only cost structure that actually makes sense.**
